title: Intent-driven quick-remediate gateway: runbook-as-task orchestration
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Objective: Build an "intent-driven quick-remediate gateway" that exposes common runbook steps as safe, auditable tasks. This ticket implements a task orchestration layer that maps intent (human- or system-initiated) into parameterized runbook subtasks with built-in safety checks, permission gating, telemetry tagging, and transparent rollback paths.

Background: On-call and support teams repeatedly run a narrow set of recovery actions (restarts, cache clears, rebalancing) that are documented in runbooks but remain manual, error-prone, and hard to audit. We want to convert those high-frequency steps into first-class tasks that: 1) are discoverable via intent (search/CLI/console), 2) can run with minimal interactive input, and 3) include safety policy checks plus automatic observability hooks.

Success criteria:
- 10 most-common runbook actions implemented as parameterized tasks with telemetry and audit logs.
- Rollout to internal SRE group with no regressions for 2 weeks.
- Mean time to remediate (MTTR) for covered incidents reduced by >=20% in pilot.

Scope:
- Core scheduler for runbook-tasks (idempotent execution, prefix/KV context propagation).
- Intent parsing surface (CLI search + Console quick actions + Slack slash command prototype).
- Safety policies: permission checks, dry-run, escalation path, rate limits, and automatic rollback hooks.
- Telemetry: attach incident IDs, user keys, and request traces to metrics and logs.

Non-goals: Full player pipeline or converting large playbooks end-to-end. Not replacing the full runbook authoring UX (design will follow incrementally).

Design notes:
- Task model: small immutable task descriptor (name, inputs, safe-defaults, validation schema, required-permissions, rollback-spec). Tasks are executed by the existing admin-runlet agent with a thin orchestration shim to ensure consistent audit headers.
- Intent mapping: simple alias table + fuzzy search on runbook titles/tags; for prototype we will surface suggestions, not auto-invoke.
- Safety: tasks must declare a "danger level" (none/low/medium/high) and require either elevated approval or canary guardrail when medium/high.
- Audit & telemetry: every task run emits a structured event (task.name, inputs.hash, user, incident_id, execution_outcome) to the central telemetry pipeline.

Implementation plan:
1) Author task descriptors for 10 high-frequency actions (2w).
2) Implement orchestration shim in ops-api to dispatch to admin agent + attach audit headers (1w).
3) Add permission checks and optional two-step approval flow for high-risk tasks (1w).
4) Build Console quick-actions UI and CLI search hook (design+FE; 2w).
5) Pilot with SRE, iterate based on telemetry and safety incidents (2w).

Telemetry & metrics:
- New metrics: task_runs_total{task, outcome}, task_latency_ms{task}, task_rollback_invoked{task}.
- Dashboards: per-task success rates and per-user run volumes.

Security & compliance: Requires security review due to privilege elevation surface and audit record implications. Integrate KMS-signed approvals for high-risk actions and retention of audit logs in compliance storage.

Rollout: staged internal rollout (alpha SRE -> broader Infra -> company-wide opt-in). Canary gating via feature-flag and limited concurrency quotas.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit and e2e tests for task descriptor validation and rollback execution.
- Docs: PRD + runbook-to-task conversion guide + runbook test harness.
- Security sign-off on approval flow and audit retention policy.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Kickoff with SRE and support: identified 12 candidate actions; prioritized top 10 (cache-clear, pod-rescale, service-restart, config-roll-forward, quota-reset, index-repair, shard-relocate, traffic-shift, db-connection-reset, feature-toggle-flip). - Ava

2026-03-03 - Engineering spike: landed a prototype task descriptor schema and a small dispatcher shim that forwards to admin-agent with X-Runbook-Context headers. Prototype repo: github.com/redwood-inference/ops-fast-path/pull/42 - Rohit

2026-03-05 - Design sync: Console team proposed a compact 'quick actions' dropdown; FE will implement item selection + confirm modal with danger-level callout. Need copy for confirm modal. - Lina (Design)

2026-03-07 - Security review kickoff: flagged key issues: ephemeral elevation tokens, approval replay protection, and audit log tamper-resistance. Security requested integration with existing KMS-backed approval signer. Action: schedule deep review next week. - Priya (Security)

2026-03-09 - Decision: implement 2-tier approvals for "high" danger tasks (1) automatic canary run on 5% of target entities, 2) manual approval if canary fails. Trade-off: slows high-risk remediation but reduces blast radius. - Rohit

2026-03-10 - QA smoke: ran 30 simulated task runs against staging with seeded failures; rollback hook invoked correctly in 4 failure cases. Found flaky retry on one agent (agent v1.18); created dependency ENG-864210 to bump agent handshake timeout. - QA
